privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Shelfmark is a personal project that stores the links you save. This page explains what we keep and why, in plain words.

store.title: What we store
store.account: From Google or GitHub: your name, email address and avatar. They are used only to sign you in and to show who is signed in. Your account record also holds the link to your Google or GitHub account (provider and account id). We do not store the access tokens from Google or GitHub.
store.content: Your links, titles, notes, folders and tags, and when you last opened a link.
store.feedback: Your answers to the in-app rating, linked to your account: a score from 1 to 10 and, if you write one, a comment.
store.sessions: For each session: when it expires, plus the IP address and the browser (user agent) it was started from, to keep sessions secure.
store.logs: Our API logs the request method, path, status and a request id, without link contents or personal data. Our host, Vercel, keeps standard request logs, including IP addresses, for a limited time.

cookies.title: Cookies and browser storage
cookies.necessary: We use strictly necessary cookies only. A session cookie keeps you signed in, in the demo as well. A short-lived cookie protects the Google and GitHub sign-in flow. They are httpOnly and SameSite, Secure on the live site, and signing out removes the session cookie.
cookies.none: There are no advertising, analytics or tracking cookies.
cookies.storage: Your browser's local storage holds interface preferences only, such as the theme and, as those features arrive, the cards or list view and the state of the Recently opened panel. They are not sent to our servers.

dont.title: What we don't do
dont.sell: We don't sell or share your data and don't show ads.
dont.read: We don't look at your saved links except where needed to operate the service, for example to fetch a preview.

previews.title: Link previews
previews.body: When you save a link, our server fetches that page to read its title and the address of its icon. The site therefore sees our server's IP address and the user agent "ShelfmarkBot", not your IP address.

limits.title: Rate limits
limits.body: Requests are rate-limited to keep the service available. Where the demo is offered, creating a demo is limited per IP address.

where.title: Where it lives
where.hosting: The API runs in Vercel's fra1 (Frankfurt) region and the database on Neon in eu-central-1 (Frankfurt). Static files are served from Vercel's global network.
where.signin: Sign-in goes through Google or GitHub, both US companies, each under its own privacy policy:

demo.title: Demo mode
demo.body: Where the demo is offered, it creates a temporary sandbox with sample links and no personal data from you. A temporary cookie keeps you in the sandbox, and the sandbox is deleted automatically after 24 hours.

control.title: Your control and retention
control.export: Where available, you can export your links, folders, tags and notes as JSON or as a browser bookmarks file (HTML).
control.delete: You can delete any link at any time, or delete your whole account in Settings, where available. Your account and all its data are then removed from the database.
control.retention: We keep your data for as long as you have an account. The database provider may keep backups for a short recovery period after deletion.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You have the right to access your data, to export it, to have it corrected or deleted, and to complain to your data protection authority. Use the in-app export and account deletion where available, or get in touch below.
rights.basis: [Legal basis for processing: to be added by the project owner.]

contact.title: Contact
contact.issues: For general questions, open an issue in the project repository. Do not post personal data in a public issue.
contact.link: Open the project issues on GitHub
contact.private: For requests involving personal data, a private contact channel will be listed here.
